info.title: Pizza 4P's POS Till API
info.description: The `/api` surface the till, the kitchen display and POS Station call on a store's edge, generated from the handlers (ADR-0177). A device presents its pairing token as a bearer token, and most routes also need a person signed in on it. A refusal is plain text, with its AIP-193 reason in the `pos-error-reason` header where the edge names one.

post.summary: `POST /api/activate` — exchange the code, store the credential, record the completion.

requestBody.description: `code`, the activation code printed on the store's setup sheet, in any casing or spacing

200.description: Activated: the `device_id` the stored credential authenticates as. The edge restarts a moment later so its cloud loops start with the credential

400.description: The code is malformed (`ACTIVATION_CODE_MALFORMED`)

401.description: Refused by the cloud (`ACTIVATION_REFUSED`), saying nothing of whether the code was spent, revoked or never real

403.description: Refused by the cloud (`ACTIVATION_REFUSED`), saying nothing of whether the code was spent, revoked or never real

404.description: Refused by the cloud (`ACTIVATION_REFUSED`), saying nothing of whether the code was spent, revoked or never real

409.description: This box already holds a credential (`ALREADY_ACTIVATED`), or the cloud says the device is in the wrong state (`ACTIVATION_WRONG_STATE`)

500.description: Activation failed

503.description: The cloud or the key vault is unavailable (`ACTIVATION_UNAVAILABLE`)

post.x-public-reason: an activation code from the store's setup sheet (ADR-0050)

get.summary: `GET /api/activation` — report whether this box holds a device credential yet.

200.description: `activated`: whether this box holds a device credential yet; and `state_access`, whether the store's state is closed to other local accounts, where the edge reports it

503.description: The key vault could not be read (`ACTIVATION_UNAVAILABLE`)

get.x-public-reason: nothing: it says only whether this box is activated yet

get.summary: `GET /api/bills/{id}/check` — what one bill owes, where it has got to, and the lines it covers.
get.description:
The read a split needs ([ADR-0128](../../../../docs/adr/0128-a-bill-splits-and-merges.md)). Once a
table's bill is split, the table read answers for every part still open, and the guest at the
till is asking about **theirs** — so the till reads the part it is about to settle, by its id.
Same [`Edge::bill_totals`](crate::app::Edge::bill_totals) the settle path assembles from.

200.description: What one bill owes, in the shape `GET /api/orders/{id}/check` answers with, plus its `state` and the `order_line_ids` it covers

400.description: The id is not a ULID

401.description: This device is not paired: no token, or one the edge does not accept

403.description: Nobody is signed in on this device, or the sign-in lapsed

409.description: The edge knows no such bill (`UNKNOWN_BILL`), or its figures cannot be assembled. `pos-error-reason` names why

post.summary:
`POST /api/bills/{id}/fees/{fee_id}/waive` — waive one of an open bill's fees, citing a reason
(ADR-0159 decision 5).
post.description:
Answers with the bill as it now stands, in the shape of its check, so the till redraws it from
the edge's arithmetic and never subtracts the fee itself: the fee's tax goes with it. A fee
that is not waivable answers `409 FEE_NOT_WAIVABLE`, one the bill does not charge
`409 FEE_NOT_ON_BILL`, and a bill that is not open `409 TRANSITION_REFUSED`.

requestBody.description: `reason_code_id`, with `approver_code` and `approver_pin` of somebody who may waive the fee where the person acting may not. Both are secrets and are never logged

200.description: What the bill now owes, in the shape `GET /api/orders/{id}/check` answers with, from the edge's own arithmetic

400.description: An id is not a ULID

401.description: This device is not paired: no token, or one the edge does not accept

403.description: Nobody is signed in on this device, or the sign-in lapsed; the waive needs an approval that was missing or refused, or the approver is locked out; or this box was superseded by a replacement

409.description: Refused: the fee is not waivable (`FEE_NOT_WAIVABLE`), the bill does not charge it (`FEE_NOT_ON_BILL`), the bill is not open, or the person lacks the permission. `pos-error-reason` names which

500.description: The edge could not apply the command

503.description: The store is unavailable, and nothing was recorded

post.summary:
`POST /api/bills/{id}/merge` — fold other bills into this one, which survives
([ADR-0128](../../../../docs/adr/0128-a-bill-splits-and-merges.md) decision 5).
post.description:
The path names the **target**: it is the bill the cashier is standing in front of, and it keeps
its identity. Every absorbed bill must be open and on the same table, which is a floor
restriction rather than a model one — settling moves a table, and a bill over two tables makes
"which table moved?" a question with two answers — and of the same order, which two counter
bills, sharing no table, need too: a settle charges a bill's lines from its own order, so
another order's would be charged nothing. Each is refused `409` before anything is written.

requestBody.description: `absorbed_bill_ids`: at least one open bill, on the same table and order, to fold into this one

200.description: Merged: the `bill_id` of the bill that survives, the one the path names

400.description: The id is not a ULID, or no bill is named to fold in

401.description: This device is not paired: no token, or one the edge does not accept

503.description: The store is unavailable, and nothing was recorded

post.summary:
`POST /api/bills/{id}/split` — partition a bill's lines into two or more bills
([ADR-0128](../../../../docs/adr/0128-a-bill-splits-and-merges.md)).
post.description:
No manager and no PIN, unlike the void beside it: a split partitions amounts that are already
captured and creates, forgives and moves nothing (decision 6). Everything that can refuse it is
the domain's — the bill must be open, and the parts must be a partition of what it covers.

requestBody.description: `parts`: two or more lists of the order line ids, each the lines one new bill covers

200.description: Split: the new `bill_ids`, in the order the parts were given

post.summary:
`POST /api/bills/{id}/void` — void a bill before it settles, citing a reason from the store's
managed list (ADR-0115, roadmap B2.2).
post.description:
Always needs a manager's PIN: a bill is money whether or not the kitchen started, so unlike a
line there is no unfired shape to let through. A settled bill is refused by the bill machine —
reversing one is a refund, with its own permission and its own reason.

requestBody.description: `reason_code_id`, a void reason from the managed list, with `approver_code` and `approver_pin`, which a bill void always needs. Both are secrets and are never logged

200.description: Voided: the `state` the bill came to rest in

post.summary: `POST /api/lines/{id}/quantity` — change how many, while the line is still editable.
post.description:
A non-positive quantity is refused here rather than by the domain, and the distinction is
deliberate: zero is not a business rule anybody argued about, it is a malformed request, in the
same class as a path segment that is not a ULID. "Take this off the order" is a **void** — a
different act, with its own event, its own reason code and its own permission once the kitchen
has seen it — and a quantity of zero must not become a quiet way to perform one.

parameters.description: The order line's id, a ULID

requestBody.description: `quantity`, in thousandths, greater than zero

200.description: The line: `order_id`, `order_line_id`, its `state`, and `station_id` once fired

post.description:
The counter's route, and the one that makes takeaway revenue collectable: a relayed or QR-counter
order is tableless by design (ADR-0064), so `/api/tables/{id}/bill` can never reach it
([ADR-0093](../../../../docs/adr/0093-bill-keyed-on-order.md)). A floor order billed through here
still makes its table's `Occupied → AwaitingPayment` move, because the domain decides that from
the order, not from which route was called.

get.summary: `GET /api/orders/{id}/check` — the running check for one order, table or no table.
get.description:
The counter's read. A takeaway order sits on no table

post.summary: Mints the code for the next device, replacing whatever code was live.
post.description:
# Why this route exists

A code is minted once per process start and nothing else minted another, so adding a second till
to a trading store meant restarting the service — which drops every till's and kitchen display's
`/ws` session and forces the outbox to drain
([ADR-0117](../../../../docs/adr/0117-a-headless-store-keeps-a-log.md) §70). This removes all but
the first of those restarts: the first device on a virgin box still uses the boot code, because
it has nothing to authenticate with, and every device after it is minted for from inside the
store.

# What it deliberately does not do

It writes **no file** and logs **no code**. `POS_EDGE_PAIRING_FILE` is the headless *boot* path
and this caller is neither headless nor booting — it is a manager holding a tablet that just
received the reply. Minting does unlink that file, because the code it named is now dead
([`Pairing::mint`]).

The log line carries no employee id either. A durable log records identifiers and counts, and a
per-employee managerial-activity stream on a shop-floor box is the thing ADR-0117 §6 kept off
disk; who admitted a device is answered by the durable pairing record, not by this line
([ADR-0118](../../../../docs/adr/0118-one-credential-per-box-and-the-cloud-learns.md) §5).

# What it records for later

The [`Minter`] rides on the code, and the redemption splits it: the **device** this request came
from is named on the cloud-bound `device.admission.granted` event, and the **employee** signed in
on it is written to the store's own `paired_devices` row and goes no further. Both facts are
known only here, at mint time — the tablet that redeems presents six digits and nothing else.

200.description: The six-digit `code` the next device presents, replacing any live one, and `expires_at_ms`. This reply is the only place the code exists: it is neither written to a file nor logged

401.description: This device is not paired: no token, or one the edge does not accept

403.description: Nobody is signed in on this device, or the sign-in lapsed; or the person's role does not grant managing devices

503.description: The OS entropy source is unavailable, so no code was minted

`GET /api/pair/devices` — which devices are paired, when each paired, and whether that survives a
restart.
get.description:
The list used to be a bare count, which left an operator with a lost tablet nothing to act on:
`POST /api/pair/revoke` takes a device id, and no surface anywhere handed one out
(production-readiness **O1**). The pairing instant is the only handle the edge has on *which*
tablet a row is — the device's name lives in the cloud's approved-device registry, and a store
that has never synced has none — so the console shows when each paired and marks the caller's own
row, which together are enough to recognise the odd one out.

The token digest is never returned: it correlates a device across restarts and buys the console
nothing the id does not.

([ADR-0158](../../../../docs/adr/0158-the-till-enforces-each-persons-own-permissions.md)
decision 8). It used to need a paired device alone, on the reasoning that the edge had no
operator identity offline; it has one now — the staff roster the cloud publishes, checked here
with no network — and retiring every till in the store is too strong an act to leave to any
tablet in the shop. Every retirement is still recorded in the log.

`GET /api/pair/this_device` — whether the calling token is still accepted, and which device it
belongs to.
get.description:
POS Station's token probe
([ADR-0158](../../../../docs/adr/0158-the-till-enforces-each-persons-own-permissions.md)
decision 8, step 1). It answers for the calling token **alone**: its device id and when it
paired, and nothing about any other device. [`paired_devices`] answered the same question by
handing every paired device the id of every other, which a probe has no use for and which
decision 8 stops once no Station that reads the list is left.

Behind the paired-device gate alone, for the reason the list is: Station asks with nobody signed
in. The route never reaches the signed-in gate, which is the only code that reads or touches a
session, so asking it signs nobody in and resets nobody's idle window.

An unknown or retired token is refused `401` by the gate, before this runs. A token retired in
the moment between the gate and the lookup below is refused the same way, because by the time the
answer is written it is no longer accepted. The device comes from the gate and never from the
request, so a router that lost the gate fails the request `500` rather than answer for nobody.

claim (`HELD_BY_ANOTHER_DEVICE`) already would.

named apart, so the card can release it.

post.summary: `POST /api/tables/{id}/seat` — seat guests and open an order.
post.description:
The body is optional, and read as raw [`Bytes`] rather than through `Json` so that it is
optional in the way devices actually behave: `Option<Json<_>>` treats a body as absent only when
the `content-type` header is missing, and plenty of clients send `application/json` with nothing
after it. Both spellings of "no count" are accepted; a body that is present but malformed is
refused rather than silently ignored, because a device that meant to send a count and got the
shape wrong should be told.

No screen prompts for the count yet — whether tap-to-seat should grow a step is roadmap **Q7**'s
call, not this slice's; the route carries it so that decision does not also need a wire change.

requestBody.description: Optional `guest_count`. An empty body seats the table with the count unknown

get.summary: Upgrades `GET /ws` to a WebSocket and pumps the fan-out into it.
get.description:
Reached only through the paired-device gate: an unpaired host on the store LAN is refused `401`
before this runs. Until S0c that gate was absent and this endpoint served the whole
committed-event stream — orders, bills, settlements — to anyone who could route to the box.

parameters.name: stream_id
parameters.description: The stream the device's last applied frame is on, to resume after it

parameters.name: after_sequence
parameters.description: The sequence of that frame. Sent with stream_id or not at all

parameters.name: Sec-WebSocket-Protocol
parameters.description: `pos-edge.v1` and, from a browser, the device token, which cannot travel in Authorization on an upgrade

101.description: Upgraded: the device receives the store's live frames, resumed after the named position where the fan-out can

401.description: This device is not paired: no token, or one the edge does not accept

403.description: The request comes from an origin the edge does not permit

till_session.description: The token a device is issued when it is paired, presented as a bearer token. On `/ws` a browser offers it as the second WebSocket subprotocol instead, because an upgrade cannot carry an Authorization header.
